from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Cone", [
            "A right circular cone forms the base shape.",
            "Introduce the cutting plane slicing through the cone.",
            "Rotate the plane to change the shape created."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=2.5, direction=DOWN).set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        plane = Surface(
            lambda u, v: np.array([u, v, 0]),
            u_range=[-1.5, 1.5], v_range=[-1.5, 1.5]
        ).set_color(BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        intersection = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FF00FF").rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.75, color=YELLOW).set_opacity(0.4)
        focus_dot = Dot(color=RED)
        focus_label = Text("Focus", font_size=16, color=RED)
        circle_label = Text("Circle", font_size=16, color="#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(cone, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(cone))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.place_at_grid(intersection, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(intersection), Write(circle_label.next_to(intersection, RIGHT)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        self.place_at_grid(focus_dot, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(focus_dot), Write(focus_label.next_to(focus_dot, UP)))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Light: Dandelin Spheres and Conic Sections

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Cone
sections.content: Define a right circular cone and introduce the 'Cutting Plane' concept. Visualize how slicing a cone at different angles yields circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
sections.example: Imagine a flashlight beam hitting a wall: rotate the flashlight to see the spot shape change from a circle to an ellipse.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres tucked inside the cone, tangent to both the cone and the cutting plane. Explain that the points of tangency are the mathematical keys to understanding conic sections.
sections.example: Picture two rubber balls (spheres) trapped inside a hollow ice cream cone, squeezed until they perfectly touch the interior surface and the cutting plate.

sections.title: The Geometric Bridge: Proving the Focus
sections.content: Show that the point where a Dandelin sphere touches the cutting plane is exactly the focus of the conic section. Use line segments from the surface of the cone to prove the distance properties (e.g., sum of distances to foci is constant for ellipses).
sections.example: Use a 3D animation where a 'fox' (the focus) stands exactly at the tangency point, highlighting how the symmetry of the sphere dictates the curve's path.

sections.title: Visualizing Different Conics
sections.content: Demonstrate the transition: 1. Ellipse (sphere is between vertex and plane), 2. Parabola (plane parallel to slant height), 3. Hyperbola (plane cuts both halves of the cone).
sections.example: A 3D laser scanner device scanning a statue: show how moving the laser angle transforms the 'scan field' from a circle to a complex hyperbola.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap: Dandelin spheres turn abstract equations into tangible 3D geometry. Relate this to satellite orbits (Kepler’s laws) and architectural design.
sections.example: A satellite (like Sputnik) orbiting Earth follows an elliptical path defined by the same geometric principles as our Dandelin sphere derivation.
